newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks zoom to record close.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks zoom to record close.

text.p: Mexican stocks soared to a record Tuesday after foreign investors flooded the market to buy stocks and on expectations primary interest rates were about to fall to their lowest level since the December 1994 peso devaluation crisis.
"Foreigners entered the market in droves, floor activity was really heavy today," a trader from the Arka brokerage said.
The leading IPC share index ended up 70.90 points, or 1.93 percent, at 3,750.03. Volume was heavy at 164 million shares traded.

A Reuters survey of nine money market traders predicted an average assignment rate of 20.30 percent for bellwether 28-day Cetes, or Treasury bills, at the central bank's weekly primary auction of government securities. This would be a fall of 1.15 percentage points since last week's auction.
Analysts said the market was helped by a recovery by market heavyweight Telmex and positive technical signals.
Telmex L shares ended up 48 centavos (6 cents) at 15.24 pesos ($1.96), while its ADRs gained 1 to 39 in New York trading.
Telmex had opened down 34 centavos (4 cents) at 14.52 pesos ($1.86) on a cool reaction to its fourth quarter earnings, posted after the close of trade on Monday.
"Opinions seem to be quite at variance on Telmex. Most were surprised by the report, but it was grist to the mill for a brave few," one trader said.
Dealers said increased participation by international investors could be seen in benchmark 48-hour peso contracts, which closed 0.4 peso firmer at 7.7935 per dollar.
On the broad market, 122 stocks traded, of which gainers trounced decliners by 78 to 22.
The most heavily traded gainer was retail stock Gigante, but after a single cross trade.

Telmex accounted for the second largest number of shares traded, followed by financial stock GFB, which ended up 18 centavos (2 cents) at 3.11 pesos (40 cents). Traders said the stock was recovering after being hit hard following its 1996 earnings report.
Other notable gains were retail stock Cifra, up 26 centavos (3 cents) at 11.32 pesos ($1.42) and cement maker Cemex, up 1.50 pesos (19 cents) to 34.00 pesos ($4.36).
